# Storage conversion map (#1002, wave 3)

This is a source inventory at Git base `ff02c9d4ea4b40564c2008cb0cf6e8bd374ee804` (2026-11-09), not a measurement of the live databases. No runtime implementation, live state, retention policy, deployment or cutover changes here. The issue's 38 destination tables are the destination; the named source variants below partition their rows. Variant spellings are proposed Rust identifiers, not assigned persisted discriminants. A source may split into several destinations as described in the special contracts below.

## Coverage

| Database   | Catalog application tables | Additional current application tables | Mapped | Unmapped |
| ---------- | -------------------------: | ------------------------------------: | -----: | -------: |
| Canvas     |                        110 |                                     8 |    118 |        0 |
| Analytics  |                         17 |                                     1 |     18 |        0 |
| Supervisor |              not cataloged |                                     8 |      8 |        0 |
| Total      |                        127 |                                    17 |    144 |        0 |

Canvas additions: `approvals`, `task_window_state`, `agent_publication_state`, `project_grants`, `runtime_work_results`, `runtime_work_decisions`, `runtime_work_releases`, `runtime_online_migration_dirty` (`runtime_peer_update_settings` is cataloged since the db-api pilot, f9535770). Analytics adds `analytics_publication_overflow_receipts`. Supervisor has seven tables in `supervisor_schema.sql` plus `operation_writes` in `supervisor_journal.rs:122`. FTS shadows, SQLite internals and six historical/staging names are classified separately; they do not add application destinations.

The coverage witness is `node --test workspaces/tooling/apps/repository-checks/tests/storage-map.test.ts`; `package.json` includes it in `test:tooling` and `test:tooling:js`, which the fast gate consumes. It checks exactly one dedicated contract and one manifest row per source, all 38 targets, and mutation witnesses for missing and duplicate entries. It guards all 127 catalog tables and an explicit inventory of 17 code-created tables (8 Canvas, 1 Analytics, 8 Supervisor), not semantic completeness or automatically discovered future lazy tables. The mutation witness omits each of those 17 tables in turn.

## Wave-3 source-to-target manifest

This manifest supersedes the single-destination arrows in the stage-1 contracts below. It has **144 source rows: Canvas 118, Analytics 18, Supervisor 8**, and exactly **38 destination tables: 26 / 7 / 5**. Counts describe source tables, never live record counts. Source keys, columns, SQL sites, trigger predicates and original codecs remain specified in the corresponding dedicated contract below; those contracts are part of each manifest row. The source inventory is unchanged at origin/main `9446659aae8d2002deca8cd47f6820e732f6b691`. Current descriptor ownership is checked against the read-only wave-2 `land-w2c 7c8742b2` snapshot: `canvas_schema.rs::registry` registers 69 descriptors; Analytics and Supervisor have no corresponding registry there. Wave-2 keeps physical layouts, so its descriptor owners replace the older inferred owner names without changing this inventory.

**Kind owner:** the qualified names below are the proposed db-api `DbEnum` owners and variants for wave 3, not existing persisted codes. Each target has one enum owner shared by its descriptors, payload discriminator and validators; implementation assigns explicit stable INTEGER discriminants. Dedicated tables are marked unpartitioned: source names there are merge inputs, not invented kind columns. The incident/event/status/codec enums of dedicated tables keep their existing separate owners. `request_results` likewise retains typed receipt alternatives rather than gaining a source-kind key that could weaken request-ID uniqueness and signature matching. Supervisor state keys stay open. All proposed names and unresolved contracts require implementation review before cutover.

**K0 — identity:** preserve the complete listed key and original SQLite storage classes. Kind namespaces prevent collisions across source families; encode composite components with type tags and lengths, never delimiter concatenation. Nonunique owner/ordinal pairs remain nonunique. Original rowid is authoritative for keyless cost groups and revision-clock rows, and remains migration evidence elsewhere. Copy cursors do not replace logical identity; the positive-i64 adapter remains unproven (U5).

**K1 — nullable legacy identity:** SQLite rowid-table TEXT/composite primary keys can admit NULL and repeated NULL tuples. Never coalesce to empty IDs, replace a row or deduplicate it. A collision-safe proposed migration identity is a tagged original-key tuple plus original source rowid for these rows, under the source partition; retain the original nullable key separately in that variant's typed evidence. This is the selected lossless layout (L2), including tagged identities for orphan merge inputs; original caller lookups remain on the retained original key. WITHOUT ROWID and genuine INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rows do not have that particular NULL-key ambiguity. No live key validation is claimed.

**T0 — clocks:** preserve every owner unit, precision, nullability and clock domain from the per-column contract. Sequence, generation, revision, epoch, offset and ACK are counters, never wall time. JSON times and physical times are distinct. REAL wall times remain original fractional Unix seconds pending E1; the proposed INTEGER target does not authorize rounding or a unit change. INTEGER times retain their documented seconds/milliseconds, and process start ticks retain ticks. REAL token amounts remain nullable fractional counts. Existing absence/default selectors do not invent original time values.

**C0 — codecs:** retain exact source TEXT/BLOB storage and bytes through the named per-column owner in the contract, including StoredText compression/dictionaries, exact replies, presence-aware Field, and raw unknown JSON inside named typed payloads. Wave-2 ExactJson/JsonRecordCodec owners below are conversion inputs; do not reserialize original evidence from selectors. Scalar and enum classification in the final correction section takes precedence over early inferred payload names. L10 resolves known admission mismatches with typed raw-evidence alternatives; U2/U3 still require owner-specific validation for every typed conversion.

**X0 — callers:** R/W are representative production input owners, with paths relative to runtime-store (S) and runtime-services (V). The full R/W/DDL list, generic dispatch ledger, dynamic Table callers and direct TypeScript/embedded-helper SQLite consumers below are mandatory for each row. Wave-2 descriptors take precedence over stale line numbers; their business callers and retained raw queries are listed in the wave-2 family ledgers. In particular upgrade-canary watermarks, installed-smoke accounting and chat-scale joins must migrate alongside their source families. No literal hit is not proof of no reader or writer.

**D0 — deletion:** preserve each source's explicit service deletion predicates, retention, and all indexed/triggered cascades in its contract and SQL-site ledger. Shared targets must restrict deletion to the exact kind and original owner/key; never fan a generic owner deletion into unrelated kinds. Preserve the same source-change/publication tombstones and transaction boundary. No new blanket cascade or retention is introduced. Parents delete dependents first; permission revocation and receipt expiry remain their original policies. The named triggers below identify additional cross-table obligations, not permission to drop check triggers.

### Split and merge obligations

- **agents + chats → agents:** merge by original agent identity, not row position; preserve chat-row presence and nullable auto-wake/usage-resume/execution-mode/epoch independently of agent-record fields. Q15 re-parenting remains existing behavior. L5 retains orphan/conflict inputs in presence-aware typed legacy components; do not synthesize a current chat or overwrite either source.
- **groups → entities + relations:** the Group entity retains id/name and original member-list evidence. GroupMember relations use (group identity, original list ordinal), with member identity as an indexed endpoint; repeated members and order survive. graph_edges remains a distinct GraphEdges partition with its own (source,target,kind) uniqueness. L4 retains malformed or non-list historical membership as typed raw evidence; it never becomes an empty group.
- **queue events + metadata + revisions → queue_events:** metadata and revision are separate presence-aware typed components joined by event id. Preserve revision-only tombstone identities after event deletion and missing metadata versus an empty metadata object. L6 permits a typed revision-only row without fabricating a live queue event.
- **search metadata → items; search → search:** retain the exact item/search-rowid bijection and original search kind/agent. L7 keeps a presence-aware legacy search-metadata component for absent items and unattached FTS identities. The search engine owns its shadows; rebuilding requires checked item identities, not copying shadows as application rows.
- **user_terminals → terminals + terminal_chunks:** keep terminal metadata separate from inline output; retain the original inline-output presence and output-generation/offset semantics. Existing user_terminal_output rows keep (terminal,start), Unicode-scalar boundaries, and bytes. Do not append inline output again over already retained chunks; prove the overlap reconciliation against the original generation before cutover. Decoder bytes and event ACK use distinct streams partitions.
- **voice_records → history + contents:** every original voice record remains a VoiceRecords history entry; only retained audio bytes, if any, become VoiceAudio contents with an exact reference from the original record. Text-only records do not fabricate audio. Voice delivery/approval/session identities remain their separately named partitions.
- **limit-reset merge:** `limit_reset.rs:129–143` deliberately binds a new public request to an existing attempt. Retain every original request→attempt binding, not just one request per attempt. Lead decision L11 maps each binding to `Canvas.relations`, `CanvasRelationKind::LimitResetRequest` (SQL kind label `limit_reset_request`), with source=request id unique within that kind, target=attempt id, and unchanged payload/time (the current row has no time/payload columns). `limit_resets` holds only attempt-level fields; it has no single-request uniqueness requirement. Pending/uncertain and already-redeemed evidence must never authorize another reset-credit charge.
- **tool-request merge:** preserve the original managed/provider RequestKind and origin uniqueness independently of proposed source partitions. Name/alias admission records, name-target associations and speech obligations do not automatically have a tool-request actor/origin/lifecycle; L12 selects a typed source-specific admission variant and namespace-tagged storage identity without weakening retry deduplication.
- **history merges:** results, decisions, releases, room/chat messages, access/server audit, context/model facts and voice entries retain their distinct kind and original identity. Work child ids, work/idx ordering, tail truncation and parent cascade stay atomic with parent writes/tombstones; no new uniqueness on owner/ordinal. Retain chat-message autoincrement sequence as well as message id.
- **changes/publications/metadata merges:** durable rows and scheduler changes retain separate source domains and cursor floors; sync_documents/sync_entities retain publication scope/id and sequence identities. Preserve source-generation increments, old/new membership fences, hash-only transcript markers, no-op behavior and all sequence high-waters. These are transactions, not lossy event-log unions.
- **Analytics merges:** facts partitions retain original id, root/account/provider context and time/sequence; changes keep usage and cost-group revision domains separate. Metadata keeps cursor, generation, floor and overflow receipt lifetimes separate. cost_groups uses original rowid, SQL IS null matching and exact fractional tokens; cost_rows retains excluded versus unknown-model counting. Capture acknowledgement and derived facts/cost/change writes stay in the existing Analytics transaction; Canvas hand-off remains independent.
- **Supervisor handles/operations merges:** child identity and degraded proof are independently optional structs, not booleans, under handles (L8). Operation-write marker is independently present or absent evidence under operations (L9). Accepted-only after a crash is still uncertain even if child.write happened; never resend on marker absence. NativeId retains INTEGER/TEXT/absent tags; generation, digest and exact response remain distinct. Recovery history survives handle retirement; event ACK deletion stays independent of recovery retention.

### Lossless layout decisions

These decisions select layouts inside the 38 targets; they change neither original values nor feature behavior. They are not escalations. Typed legacy alternatives preserve existing read/refusal outcomes, not automatic repair. The original per-column/SQL contract remains authoritative for public lookup and admission behavior.

- **L2 — nullable and duplicate keys:** use K1's tagged original tuple plus source rowid, retaining original storage classes and NULL. Keyless revision-clock rows each retain rowid; do not collapse them into a singleton. Original logical lookup predicates remain separate from the storage identity.
- **L3 — receipts:** use a named typed receipt variant for each source and a reversible namespace-tagged storage id; keep original request id, signature, lifecycle, admission and exact reply/reference fields. Existing request_results keeps its own namespace and identity/signature conflict rule. Lookup adapters use the original request namespace; no new public identity or expiration rule is introduced.
- **L4 — groups:** ordered GroupMember rows use original list ordinal, preserving duplicates; the entity keeps exact list evidence. Malformed/non-list evidence is a typed legacy alternative with the original refusal behavior, never silently normalized.
- **L5 — agents/chats:** merge matching valid identities with independently present chat fields. Retain missing/orphan/conflicting source components in a named legacy evidence variant keyed by K1 when necessary; it does not create a runnable agent or synthetic chat. Callers preserve the old join/presence rules. Keep current re-parenting behavior (Q15).
- **L6 — queue components:** allow typed live-event, metadata-only and revision-only storage variants, retaining original component presence. Revision-only rows remain tombstones and never enter dispatch; metadata-only reads retain the original lookup behavior.
- **L7 — search:** items stores a typed legacy search-metadata component when the transcript component is absent. Retain original search_rowid uniqueness and FTS evidence, without inventing transcript text or changing which search results the old join admits.
- **L8 — supervisor proof:** handles stores independently optional child identity/degraded proof; orphan components use a typed legacy variant and original handle key. Qualified PID/start/generation checks remain unchanged; these components alone never authorize signaling or create a process handle.
- **L9 — operation write proof:** operations stores independently optional accepted-operation and written-marker components; orphan markers retain their original compound identity. No accepted row or marker is synthesized, and absent write proof keeps the original uncertainty behavior.
- **L10 — historical admission:** use named typed raw-evidence variants for arbitrary JSON and malformed historical text, preserving exact storage bytes and existing refusal/last-key-wins behavior. Preserve nonzero legacy flag values in a typed legacy-integer alternative while new boolean writes remain 0/1. These alternatives do not broaden or narrow current admission.
- **L11 — reset request bindings (lead decision):** retain every request→attempt row in relations kind=limit_reset_request, source=request id unique within the kind, target=attempt id. Payload/time are unchanged. limit_resets keeps attempt-level fields only, preserving many-to-one binding and avoiding repeat charges.
- **L12 — tool requests:** each source gets the listed DbEnum admission variant and a namespace-tagged storage key. Keep original actor/origin presence explicitly in that variant; a name target is an association, not a newly executed tool call. Preserve the original uniqueness and idempotency predicates per source kind, with managed/provider origin uniqueness unchanged.

### Explicit cutover escalations (1)

**E1 — fractional wall time:** the proposed INTEGER timestamp columns cannot generally represent existing fractional REAL/JSON Unix seconds in the owner's unchanged unit. A reversible encoding (or explicit permission to change value/unit) requires an owner decision. Until then preserve the original values and block the affected time conversion. This is a source-contract incompatibility, not a claim that live data is invalid. No rounding, seconds→milliseconds assumption or f64 bit reinterpretation is authorized. The E1 rows identify known physical/payload time owners; U1 also applies to timestamps subsequently found inside raw provider evidence.

## Value and owner rules

- Every closed Rust enum becomes INTEGER with explicit Rust discriminants that never change or reorder. Existing string enum order is not a persisted code. Closed CHECK sets below are evidence, not permission to coerce unknown history to an arbitrary variant.
- Booleans use INTEGER 0/1; nullable booleans preserve NULL. Integers retain their owner range and unit. Timestamps use INTEGER in the owner's unit only with exact preservation (U1). REAL token counts and measurements are not timestamps and must not be rounded.
- TEXT is for genuinely open text/IDs. Fixed-format validated digests/keys become BLOB after proving exact reversible encoding; arbitrary historical strings must not be silently interpreted as hex or UUIDs. Opaque original JSON, exact responses, compressed records and bytes use BLOB with their typed codec owner.
- **Owner decision: maximally strict typing immediately.** Every JSON column gets a named Rust struct/enum. No `serde_json::Value` or `studio_json::Value` enters the new persistence API or generated code. Existing named owners that contain Value are migration work, not approved target owners. Exact JSON and unknown fields use `OwnedRawJson` (or `Box<RawValue>`) inside a named typed struct, with typed known selectors and `BTreeMap<String, OwnedRawJson>` only for genuinely open extensions. Each per-column planned owner below is part of the implementation contract; its fields must come from the cited current owner, not a second schema.
- Physical SQL columns are always present. SQL NULL is not an absent JSON member. `Field<T>` is Missing / Null / Value; keep its discriminator or equivalent typed representation. `Option<T>` semantics depend on serde defaults/present adapters. A generated selector may intentionally collapse absent and explicit null, while the original typed record/evidence must retain their difference. Unknown or malformed historical values must remain original evidence and produce the current refusal/hold behavior.
- A proposed per-source `*StorageRow` names a conversion input/variant owner. Final target descriptors compose these variants under one authoritative table owner. A `*Payload` name means a named typed struct/enum with raw exact evidence inside it, never a transparent untyped JSON carrier.

## Unresolved boundaries (block the affected cutover, not this inventory)

**U1 — fractional time:** many owners store finite f64/JSON-number Unix seconds (`as_secs_f64`), including Supervisor epoch inputs. `CAST(... AS INTEGER)` loses fractional time. Integer milliseconds also need proof of precision and original-value reconstruction. No blanket seconds→milliseconds change, rounding, or bit reinterpretation is authorized by this map. The worker must prove a lossless integer encoding with the owner or retain original raw evidence and request an exact encoding decision. Negative/oversized/nonfinite historical values need explicit handling. Unit-specific notes below take precedence over column-name guesses.

**U2 — typed JSON extraction:** query-derived path lists are conservative: a multi-table SQL statement can mention another table's record. Bind each expression to its SQL alias and the cited Rust field before declaring a new column. Generated expressions, CASE defaults, `json_type`, arrays, truthiness and COALESCE are behavior, not merely extraction hints. Preserve raw original evidence as well as typed selectors; do not duplicate a Value payload. Proposed payload owners are named, but their full enum/field declarations are implementation work.

**U3 — vocabulary:** SQL TEXT alone proves no closed set. A field with no closed Rust owner/validated CHECK stays open until the conversion identifies that owner. Future/Other variants, arbitrary `&str` boundaries, historical invalid states and namespace keys must not be narrowed by observed examples. A closed target variant may retain unknown historical evidence in a typed refusal/raw-evidence branch, without changing admission rules.

**U4 — dynamic SQL and direct consumers:** the per-table SQL inventory includes literal SQL, table constants, catalog indexes/triggers and selected generic substitutions outside tests. Generic statements whose table is computed are enumerated separately below; an absence of literal SQL does not prove no consumer. Known tooling queries, migrations and service SQL are included. External ad-hoc SQLite readers cannot be proven absent from repository source. Family cutover must search its dynamic callers, preserve exact public shapes and explicitly migrate identified direct consumers.

**U5 — online copy key:** `online_migration.rs:68` supports positive i64 source keys, not arbitrary text/composite keys. Rowid tables can use an explicit rowid adapter only after positivity/stability validation; FTS and WITHOUT ROWID need their own owner path. Copying with a rowid cursor does not change the logical key. Dirty-key deletion needs the old identity after the source row is gone. Do not claim an existing generic adapter; none is implemented here.

**U6 — exact replay:** `request_results.result`, operation responses and provider receipts preserve original encoded bytes or their exact stable reference; do not reconstruct them from mutable entities. `operations.native_id` is declared INTEGER but accepts TEXT too (tagged `NativeId`); the SQL declaration alone is not its stored-value type. A missing operation-write marker is absence of proof, not proof of no effect.

## Conversion families and file ownership

F0 establishes clocks, source-change and browser-publication descriptors first. F1 and F2 then convert compatible settings/history; F3 and F4 may proceed in parallel after F0, with grants and request uniqueness preserved. F5, F6, F7, F8 and F9 are separate stage-3 work streams after F0/F1 and descriptor APIs: their source files below are private only when listed as exclusive. Receipt/source/outbox cutover is one transaction even when work is prepared in separate files. F10 follows the existing Canvas capture handshake after source parity; F11 is last and independently owned. Final retirement follows all families, interrupted-copy checks, query plans and reviewed rollback evidence. No table moves in this document.

## Generic SQL, dispatch and source ownership

The sites in this section apply in addition to per-table literal sites. A generated source query or change trigger is still a reader/writer. These files are **shared** between conversion families; one coordinator must own their edits. The table names supplied by callers are part of the query contract, not user-controlled SQL identifiers.

- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/records.rs:2713`: `Table<R>` owns generic typed JSON CRUD, list, ordered/filtered reads and JSON predicates; `records.rs:3415` owns `get_json_record` for a supplied table. Each `impl JsonRecord` binds the physical table and ID mode. In particular, external record keys (plans/event metadata) need not equal a JSON `id`.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/repositories/system_reads.rs:61,75,98`: dynamic scalar/record and agent-filtered reads; schemas and kind dispatch are the permitted table set.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/durable_seq.rs:135,148,177,213,313`: generated source INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE change triggers, visibility fences, initial/backfill marks and update-hook repair. `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/agent_volatile.rs:104,108,246` generates scheduler/transcript triggers. Their shared counters and deletion behavior must survive.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/feature_schema.rs:230` generates summary deletion tombstones. `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/schema.rs:74,117`, `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/migrations/mod.rs:2106,2174`, and `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/persistence.rs:340,351` generate enum-check columns/triggers. A generated column with no application SELECT can still own validation.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/repositories/analytics_capture.rs:12,33` binds `CaptureTable::{Agents,Turns,Items,Usage,History}` to the corresponding Analytics tables. Its generic read validates the named JSON schema. `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/repositories/analytics.rs:1198,1229,1240,1256` owns generic validation/count/group/page queries with existing numeric OFFSET behavior.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/stored_text_compaction.rs:180,278,284` copies/compares dynamic `(table,key,column)` values; permitted codecs are `runtime_item_fulltext.body` and `analytics_items.record`. Raw stored BLOBs must not be fed into ordinary TEXT/JSON readers.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/work_history.rs:35,68,80,88,102,128` binds each result/decision/release kind. `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-services/src/entity_scope.rs:1054` joins history rows to their work owner and durable marks. All three history families inherit these sites.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/online_migration.rs:158` generates migration dirty INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers for the supplied source; `:153` writes old and new keys at/below the committed mark. `:217,232,347` reads/drains dirty keys. Metadata conversion cannot invalidate its own in-progress checkpoints.
- `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/supervisor_journal.rs:770` deletes handle-owned rows by a fixed retirement table list (events, operations, operation_writes, child identities and degraded proof). Recovery audit rows have separate retention.
- Dynamic service readers/writers and their exact sites are included below as an additional dispatch ledger. Family owners must resolve runtime table selections against their descriptors before removing any old schema.

## Special conversion contracts and typed-owner gaps

Source abbreviations inside this section: `runtime-store/src` = `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src`; `runtime-schema/src` = `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src`; `runtime-services/src` = `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-services/src`. A `:line` following a named file continues that same file.

These details qualify the per-column proposals. The cited source owners remain authoritative. The names of new payload structs are planned owners; this task does not introduce them.

### Agents, turns, monitors and tasks

`AgentRecord` is `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/records.rs:346`; its indexed generated selectors are owned by `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/agent_columns.rs:120` and the current catalog. Stored `AgentStatus` (`records.rs:79,132`) has `Other(UnknownAgentStatus)`: status remains open TEXT even though a separate public schema enum is closed. `ProviderKind` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/provider_kind.rs:27`) is Codex/Claude, and `AgentExecutionMode` (`records.rs:153`) is Native/Host/Vm: these become INTEGER enums. Do not infer provider from an account key.

`AgentRecord` contains raw/historical transfer and recovery forms, not just its common typed shape. `StoredTransferValue<T>` (`records.rs:910`), `StoredTransferObject<T>` (`:930`) and `StoredStartOutcomeHold` (`:1245`) retain unreadable/unknown evidence. Replace their current Value branches with named evidence enums holding `OwnedRawJson`, preserving refusal/hold behavior. `RecoveryAgentRecord`'s `RecoveryFields.stage` is `Option<String>` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/recovery_record.rs:254`): open TEXT. Nested objects need named owners (`AgentRecoveryEvidence`, `AgentArchiveEvidence`, `AgentContextRepairEvidence`) and raw extensions, not an unrestricted Value column.

`runtime_agents` and `chats` merge by the same chat/agent identity into **one** `Canvas.agents` row, combining profile and domain fields; their source variants are not two unrelated target rows. `ChatState` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/domain.rs:68`) = Active/Paused/Archived; `SessionState` (`:129`) = Starting/Ready/Lost/Ended; `TurnState` (`:78`) = Starting/Running{session}/Completed/Failed/Interrupted. Preserve the state↔session coupling, one unfinished turn per chat, and one active attempt per chat (`domain.rs:211,221`). `TurnRow.attempt` is encoded JSON and needs a named `TurnAttemptPayload`; its optional `StartAttemptAction` selector uses INTEGER enum codes (Compact/Review/Capacity/Safety). The interrupt ticket is an open string: named `InterruptTicket(String)`, stored as TEXT with SQL NULL absence.

`runtime_agent_volatile` is a distinct write boundary. Its nine TEXT-affinity columns contain **JSON field values**, not nine arbitrary text strings (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/agent_volatile.rs:31`). `AgentLiveStorageRow` must use the existing typed counters/activity/tool/context/token owners from `AgentRecord`, with raw evidence only inside named typed wrappers for historical number/string forms. Missing and JSON null both clear these columns (`:14`), unlike general Field<T> semantics. Keep the update-if-changed predicate and scheduler/transcript effects.

`MonitorRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/monitor_record.rs:437`) owns the complete monitor. `MonitorTime(f64)` (`:11`) is fractional seconds. `MonitorStatus` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/studio_errors/monitor.rs:8`) = approval/starting/running/completed/failed/cancelled/lost. `stream_pending` is a queue nonemptiness selector; `monitor_error_candidate` encodes invalid/lost status or failed-without-integer-exit-code; `monitor_created` defaults invalid evidence to 0 for selection. Typed columns must preserve these CASE/default and error-candidate semantics. Operation/account/stream/input-attempt evidence stays in named structs (already present in monitor_record.rs); exact output belongs to its existing typed owners.

`TaskRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/task_record.rs:133`) has distinct TaskKind, TaskStatus and TaskType owners (`:12,19,33`); do not replace them with WorkStatus. `ProcessId` (`:45`) is tagged evidence rather than an unrestricted integer; task recovery holds have their own stage/outcome enums (`:75,84,90`). Keep IDs, old ordering and permissions when promoting agent/status/created selectors.

### Requests, approvals and obligations

`runtime_requests` is the published native-question/request card; `runtime_tool_requests` is managed tool lifecycle state. They do not share an accidental universal payload. `RequestRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/request_record.rs:102`) owns method/decision and raw params/preview/answer evidence. Promote agent/status/method, and `params.itemId` only for the specific request method whose index uses it.

`approvals` has RequestKind, ApprovalStateKind and CloseReason vocabularies generated by the owner in `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/approvals.rs:80`. The typed payload owners are `Request`, `Delivery`, `Detail`, `Answer`, `Deferral`, `Hidden`, `Approval` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/approvals.rs:102,350,367,273,381,390,398`). Preserve turn-optional kinds, request.kind equality, answer/command/answered_by/at/since/reason state coupling, paired deferral/hide evidence, and fire_at only while pending (`runtime-store/src/approvals.rs:84`). Lazy indexes: `approvals_turn`, `approvals_agent_open`, `approvals_account_open` (delivery.account), `approvals_fire_at`; check triggers `approvals_check_insert/update` and chat-deletion triggers are generated in `:119,145`. Promote delivery.account without erasing delivery absence. Do not infer these real-valued time units from their names.

`request_results` has three admissible shapes, not a mandatory JSON result: body-only, complete stable reference-only, and rejected-with-neither (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/migrations/m2026_11_01_request_reference_outbox.rs:29`). `StoredResult` / `ResultEnvelope<R>` / `RequestReference` are at `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/repositories/request_results.rs:47,30,63`. Proposed `StoredRequestResult` is a strict enum of these shapes, with an exact `OwnedRawJson` body and typed actor selector. IDs include derived tuple identities (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/persistence.rs:29`), so a blanket UUID BLOB conversion is invalid. `created` is Unix milliseconds; retain original issuance time, UUIDv7 age/future-skew checks, the expiry floor, and changed-signature refusal. `ref_rev` is a revision, not time. `result.actor` is an indexed optional open ID.

`command_send_admissions`, `runtime_lead_requests` and `runtime_server_inbox` enter request_results only as distinct typed receipt variants retaining their own namespace/signature/result/proof shape. This map does **not** prove their contracts identical to `ResultEnvelope<R>`. A conversion must encode those differences explicitly; no default reconstructed reply or shared cleanup policy is authorized.

`OutboxRow<P>` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/repositories/outbox.rs:8`) has Unix-ms created/next_at; generation and ordinal are counters. `OutboxKind`, `OutboxStatus`, `OwnerKind` and RestartRule (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/persistence.rs:148,151,154,191`) define kind-specific behavior. Unknown/unrecognized/cancelled require NULL next_at (`runtime-store/src/receipt_schema.rs:21`); NULL does not mean due now. `OutboxPayload` must be a strict per-kind union of existing owners, not Value. `for_owner_tagged` checks JSON **presence**, including explicit null (`outbox.rs:115,135`). `Publication<T>` (`:351`) has its own class, counters and optional overflow counts; absent count differs from Some(0).

Scheduled capacity/safety/usage-resume rows go to outbox variants, retaining cause/deadline/state and admission evidence. `UsageResumeRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/usage_resume_record.rs:11`) currently has open Field<String> cause/status: neither becomes a strict observed-value enum. Replace accountKey's current Field<Value> with a named presence-aware account identity evidence type. `runtime_limit_reset_attempts` and request→attempt bindings remain one limit_resets family with exact not-sent/written/unknown and reset-credit evidence; a missing reply cannot admit another charge.

`runtime_error_incidents` needs `IncidentStoredRecord` / per-IncidentKind payload enums; kind/owner-kind are closed, payload evidence stays exact. Its SQL times are Unix milliseconds, owned by `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/error_incidents.rs:8`; `dismissed_at=NULL` means open. `runtime_account_state` needs named `AccountStreams`, `LimitsObservation`, `AccountStartFailure` owners: generation, journal ACK and recovery_required are separate facts, and observation metadata's f64 times do not inherit receipt-ms units.

### Collaboration, history, transcript and terminal data

`WorkItem` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/work_item_record.rs:35`) has WorkStatus ready/blocked/running/review/accepted/cancelled, and presence-aware owner/agent/rootId/title. Its current results/decisions/releases/extensions contain Value. Introduce `WorkResultRecord`, `WorkDecisionRecord`, `WorkReleaseRecord` and raw extensions, retaining each child ID `{work}:{index}`, the index and the corresponding original arrays. Three `(work,idx)` indexes and `runtime_work_history_cascade` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/work_history.rs:35,41`) must survive atomically with parent writes/deletes and tombstones. `archive_next_at` uses missing/null→0 as immediately eligible; do not mistake that selector default for an original timestamp.

Workspace operations' kind/phase are closed (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/workspace_operation.rs:24,25`), but their source/provider/result/extensions currently contain Value. Proposed `WorkspaceOperationSource`, `WorkspaceOperationProviderEvidence`, `WorkspaceOperationResult` are named typed owners with raw evidence. Their restart hold is Field<bool>. Plan steps and checkpoint extensions likewise need named `PlanStepRecord` and raw extensions. `ComplaintSeconds` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/complaint_record.rs:9`) explicitly owns seconds; required-nullable complaint fields must remain required even when null.

`runtime_event_meta` needs named `EventAssetReference` and `EventTiming` in place of Value arrays/maps. Delivery uses `StoredDelivery(String)` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/delivery.rs:7`): historical queue/steer/after_tool canonicalize to current_turn and after_turn to next_turn, while preserving original spelling. An enum code alone would lose that evidence. `runtime_events.kind/status` are closed by SQL even though QueueEvent currently uses String. The child-result index extracts JSON from **text.agent_id**; make a typed child-result selector without requiring every event text to be JSON. Queue-event revisions stay in their own clock domain.

`TranscriptItemRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/transcript_record.rs:123`) has closed role assistant/user/system/output and typed TranscriptText. Physical `runtime_items.created` and JSON `at` are different times; do not equate them. Asset MIME/path/name are open; hash needs actual format validation before BLOB conversion. `runtime_item_fulltext.body` and `analytics_items.record` can be BLOB despite TEXT affinity: `StoredText` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/stored_text.rs:184`) owns plain TEXT compatibility and stored-format-1 zstd bytes with checksum/content-size/dictionary evidence (`:1,27`). Retain every dictionary and original encoded bytes; new BLOB wrappers must distinguish original plain UTF-8 from compressed bytes without heuristic decoding.

`ChatMessage.deliveries` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/records.rs:3386`) currently contains Value: use named `MessageDeliveries` with recipient→RecipientDelivery, preserving DeliveryStatus rather than substituting the merged public MessageSendStatus. Group name/identity belongs to an entities Group variant; group membership additionally becomes relations GroupMember rows, preserving the original member list evidence and order when observable. Graph edge uniqueness remains (source,target,kind).

`TerminalRecord` (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/terminal_record.rs:10`) has open Field<String> status and presence-aware integer exitCode. Extra known fields need named owners and raw extensions. Inline user_terminals.output moves to terminal_chunks; offset/output_generation stay counters. Output chunk `start`/`end` are Unicode-scalar offsets (not byte offsets), and pending decoder bytes remain BLOB. Per-terminal event ACK sequence and decoder state go to separate streams variants; do not lose incomplete UTF-8 across reconnects.

`project_grants` uses GrantRow and Capability (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/project_grants.rs:45,36`), currently only LeadMessages. Pairing capability is an INTEGER enum; grant/peer/project IDs stay open. Times created_at/revoked_at are owner milliseconds (verify creation caller before copying historical rows); NULL revoked_at means active. Preserve index `project_grants_active` and `project_grants_check_insert/update` (`:89`), including final revocation that cannot be cleared. `peer_label` was added by `migrations/m2026_11_02_project_grant_peer_label.rs:16`; empty legacy labels are retained.

Never collapse all token categories or the cache-write-1h distinction.

Publication-overflow receipt counters are monotonic saturating **counts**, not booleans: charge only the positive increment in per-receipt maxima and update CaptureErrors in the same transaction (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-services/src/analytics_capture.rs:733,758,773`).

Keep its original ID, name, created time, validated SHA-256 and dictionary bytes. Index `(name,created,id)` and `_no_update`, `_no_delete`, `_no_replace` triggers at `:43` keep retained dictionaries immutable. `runtime_stored_text_batches` (both databases) contains audit fingerprints and byte counts; lack of application SELECT does not make evidence disposable.

### Supervisor: complete handle and process identity contract

Supervisor owns a separate `supervisor.sqlite3`. Do not route its process proof or acknowledgements through Canvas transactions. All time values created/closed_at/accepted/at/recovered_at are f64 Unix seconds and need U1 resolution; process start identity is **not** a Unix timestamp.

`handles`: id/signature are String, pid u32, sequence/acknowledged/rpc_sequence/generation are u64 (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/supervisor_journal.rs:166`; snapshot owner in `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-providers/src/supervisor_protocol.rs`). `init_result` is currently `Option<Value>` and needs named `SupervisorInitResult` with exact OwnedRawJson evidence. SQL NULL means no stored init result, distinct from JSON null. `closed_at`/`closed_reason` are Option<f64>/Option<String>. Keep open historical close-reason text unless all producer values are proven closed. `created` determines the journal epoch `<journalId>:floor(created*1_000_000)` (`supervisor_journal.rs:472`): even a small rounding change can change identity.

Reserve-before-spawn inserts/updates pid=0 without recreating an already admitted child (`supervisor_journal.rs:485`). Opening resets RPC sequence/init/closure, increments or validates generation, installs identity and deletes old degraded proof in one transaction (`:518`). `start_failed` only closes the unopened reservation with the same launch signature (`:503`). Sequence and ACK are not reset arbitrarily by migration. Preserve exact signature replay/admission decisions and missing-versus-closed distinctions.

`child_identities`: handle String key, pid/pgid u32, start_time String, job_name String and job_kill_on_close bool. Current reader at `supervisor_journal.rs:330` joins start_time/pgid/pid to handles; mismatched child PID refuses (`:334`). Missing child row means no identity evidence; it must not become zeros or a synthesized verified identity. Proposed `SupervisorProcessIdentity` enum wraps the typed current process identity plus named raw legacy evidence. Identity definitions in `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-process/src/supervisor_identity.rs:3` include boot identity/start ticks or start seconds/microseconds. Preserve exact ticks and boot/session identity. Legacy strings that prove exit do not necessarily authorize signaling.

`degraded_handles` presence is qualified proof, not a boolean: prior_pid, current handle PID, child PID and start_time must agree (`supervisor_journal.rs:335`). Only already-exited/terminated/killed produce it (`:797`). A new opening deletes it; identity-mismatch never fabricates proof. Consolidated handles therefore needs an optional `SupervisorDegradedProof` struct retaining the original prior PID/start identity/recovered time.

`operations.native_id` is an **affinity exception**: declared INTEGER accepts both NativeId::Integer(i64) and NativeId::Text(String), and absence. Exact reader and writer are `supervisor_journal.rs:279,291,299`; normalizing numeric text into an integer changes identity and is refused (`:554`). New STRICT storage needs a tagged native-ID enum and corresponding INTEGER/TEXT payload. Digest matching, optional historical generation, exact optional response and response_sequence remain independent facts. `operations_monitor_native` is `(handle,generation,native_id) WHERE substr(operation_id,1,8)='monitor:'` (`:856`); retain equivalent lookup with the tag.

`operation_writes` becomes presence-aware written evidence inside operations. Acceptance and RPC increment commit before child.write; mark_written follows the actual write (`workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-process/src/supervisor_daemon.rs:510`). A crash between them can leave accepted-only evidence **after an actual write**. Missing marker is no durable proof, never permission to resend. Reusing an operation ID with different digest refuses; same digest returns its saved identity/answer. Response assignment stays handle/native-ID/generation-fenced, monitor-only and once-only (`supervisor_journal.rs:637`). Proposed `SupervisorOperationResponse` replaces current `ReceiptRecord.response: Option<Value>` (`supervisor_protocol.rs:434`) using exact raw evidence inside the typed owner.

`events` uses `StoredEvent` (`supervisor_journal.rs:183`): sequence/generation u64, `JournalEventKind::{Stdout,Stderr,Exit}`, payload OwnedRawJson; size is encoded UTF-8 JSON bytes for buffer accounting. Append validates generation/continuity and commits handle sequence with the event; ACK validates cursor, deletes through it and advances acknowledgement in one transaction (`:625,646`). Preserve raw bytes, frame sizing, legacy replay and generation fencing. Recovery audits do not enter this sequence/ACK domain. Handle retirement requires the correct generation, finished readers/exit and acknowledged output.

`recovery_events` uses original AUTOINCREMENT id, observed PID/start identity/outcome/detail and per-handle last-16 retention (`supervisor_journal.rs:793,794`). Outcomes seen in current producers include already-exited, terminated, killed, termination-failed, missing-identity and identity-mismatch; the current boundary accepts &str, so closedness remains unproven. Introduce named `SupervisorRecoveryOutcome` only with explicit historical handling; detail is open explanation. Preserve audit even after handle retirement.

`supervisor_state` has journalId and recovery key families, but ensure_journal_id accepts arbitrary keys (`supervisor_journal.rs:458`): do not narrow the stored key universe silently. `SupervisorStateValue` must be a named enum: JournalIdentity, Recovery(SupervisorRecoveryFields), and explicitly retained unknown/raw evidence. `RecoveryFields` currently uses `Field<Value>` for degraded/fallbackReady/blocked/notice (`:32`), with unrestricted object/Other forms (`:25`): replace these with typed presence-aware evidence and OwnedRawJson extensions. NULL, missing, false and malformed evidence remain distinct. Journal identity continues to namespace handle epochs.

Engine schema can depend on SQLite version; the FTS owner, not this snapshot, determines its private format. SQLite autoindexes and planner statistics likewise remain engine-owned.

## Cutover acceptance checklist for conversion workers

Each worker implements the actual caller integration for its family, plus generated descriptors, typed column selectors, and the exact codecs above. Shared schema/trigger/publication files require one coordinator; the exclusive-file lists do not authorize concurrent edits to a shared owner. Existing foreign-key-like relations may be enforced by code rather than DDL: order parent identities, child facts and publication tombstones accordingly.

Before changing the authoritative writer: compare row identities and key ranges, original-byte fingerprints, NULL/presence states, exact replies/reference revisions, operation-write evidence, retained Analytics/cost categories, deletion notes and query plans on disposable data. Prove interrupted copy and restart with the original request identities; freeze neither active user work nor the SSE cursor domains. Every composite text target uses WITHOUT ROWID and every ordinary new table is STRICT, with the explicit FTS engine exception. Retention and file shrinking remain separate decisions. After new writes, restoring an old backup loses them; require reviewed reverse-copy or forward-fix recovery before retirement. No performance improvement is claimed without the issue's measured hot-write/lock/checkpoint evidence.

## Typed-contract files in the parallel plan

The family file lists above enumerate SQL and descriptor sites. Typed-record changes also require these owners. Treat `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src/{records.rs,lib.rs,schema.rs,feature_schema.rs,migrations/mod.rs,durable_seq.rs,entity_publication.rs,runtime-state-schema.json}` and `workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src/{lib.rs,contracts.rs,persistence.rs}` as **shared coordinator files** across every participating family, even where no literal SQL identified that relationship. Generated API/catalog artifacts likewise have one coordinator; do not hand-edit generated contracts in parallel.

No new migration/persistence modules are assigned by this map: the conversion worker chooses the smallest implementation inside its family's ownership and sends shared-owner edits to the coordinator. These proposed ownership boundaries do not authorize removing another family's source column or changing public schemas independently.

## Review correction: scalar and enum classification

The source name of a column does not identify its encoding. ProviderResponseId, InterruptTicket, VoiceSessionAnswerSdp, request signatures, recovery explanations and generated open ID selectors are named string/scalar owners, not raw-JSON wrappers. Digest/public-key bytes have named byte codecs and legacy-text handling, never a JSON codec. Only actually JSON-encoded records/evidence use named typed payload structs with OwnedRawJson inside them. Open `AgentStatus::Other`, terminal status, usage-resume cause/status, search kind (which can come from an arbitrary transcript title), and process-recovery outcome remain open. Existing closed MigrationStatus, ContextRepairPhase, StartAttemptAction, RequestKind, ApprovalStateKind, CloseReason and VoiceSessionState, plus the fully enumerated private voice approval/speech producer vocabularies are explicitly INTEGER enums in their column contracts. No declaration-order codes are assigned by this document.
